about.title: Two perspectives, one outcome
about.pullquote: AI projects rarely fail on technology. They fail because nobody organises the passage from ambition to everyday practice.
paragraphs: I spent more than twenty years on the market side: as key account manager at an e-commerce agency, selling an AI-driven personalisation platform, most recently managing an international portfolio for compliance software across EMEA. Those years taught me one thing above all: organisations do not buy technology. They buy the resolution of a problem they often have not yet named precisely.

In 2020 I deliberately rebuilt my methodological foundation and completed thirteen certifications within roughly a year — project management, business analysis, agile methods, IT strategy. Not as a collection, but because I wanted to master the other half: not only to explain what a system can do, but to be accountable for it actually being implemented. Immediately afterwards I led the introduction of a laboratory information system as IT project manager.

That same principle — evidence over assertion — is what I applied to the technical side of AI in 2026: in a part-time AI Consultant certification program, I am deepening prompt engineering, working with AI models, and hands-on workflow automation. Each module closes with a graded practical exam — the program is due to complete in August 2026.

An AI project has clearly distinct roles: one that clarifies need and goal and translates between leadership, IT and the business; one that collects, structures and makes data available; one that connects models and interfaces into a usable application; and two more that build and statistically validate their own learning models. I fully cover the first of these roles — AI manager — with 25+ years as a bridge-builder between leadership, IT, legal and the business. I am actively building out the technical delivery side: in my AI Consultant certification program I have already completed several self-built, top-scoring practical projects — including a multimodal AI prototype and a production code contribution to a team software migration. I bring adjacent data experience from earlier roles and current projects, and continue to deepen modern data infrastructure. For building custom learning models, I partner with specialised data scientists and ML engineers. For organisations, that means an experienced point of contact for needs assessment and steering, with technical delivery capability that is now concretely evidenced — so far from training, not yet from a client engagement.

Today I advise organisations on AI strategy, process automation and digital transformation — with deep expertise in the EU AI Act, where regulation becomes a strategic question. Most organisations do not even know which AI systems they already run — and have been subject to deployer obligations since February 2025.

What interests me in this work is the moment an abstract requirement turns into a concrete list a team can pick up on Monday morning. Everything before that is preparation; everything after it is craft.

principles.title: Inventory before strategy

principles.title: Measurable or not at all

projects.title: Selected projects
projects.lead: Evidence rather than assertion — situation, approach, result.

items.title: AI Roadmap for a First-Contact and Qualification Assistant
items.client: Training project · WBS module KIUSCA (fictional case company)
items.challenge: An owner-run real estate and financial advisory firm was drowning in first-contact inquiries that had to be manually classified, checked for missing information and prioritised — time that was missing from actual advisory work.
items.approach: Built a complete AI roadmap rather than a point solution: use-case assessment with a consultant scorecard and impact-effort matrix, an MS365-adjacent target architecture with human-in-the-loop, a four-week MVPoc with clear target metrics, and a red/amber/green governance gate that keeps decision authority firmly with people.
items.result: 100 out of 100 points (completeness/methodology 40/40, strategy/reasoning 40/40, client orientation/pitch 20/20). The examiner specifically praised the clean separation of “evidenced”, “hypothesis” and “open”, and the traffic-light governance system. Training project from the WBS AI Consultant program, not a real client engagement — shows the methodology is directly transferable to real mandates.

items.title: Automated Intake and Governance Workflow for First-Contact Inquiries
items.client: Training project · WBS module KIAUPRO (fictional case company)
items.challenge: The roadmap designed in the prior training project needed to move from concept to an actually working, automated system — including error handling, monitoring and a solid economic case.
items.approach: Analysed the process with SIPOC and 5-Whys, then implemented a 21-node workflow in n8n: an AI agent with structured output classifies processing risk and missing information, a switch automatically routes to review, follow-up or governance review, with dedicated error paths for every critical component.
items.result: 94% score (“convincing”), with a calculated ROI of roughly 131% over six months. Training project from the WBS AI Consultant program, not a real client engagement — the first concretely built evidence for the automation capability behind the value proposition.

items.title: Hybrid AI Architecture for a Hardware Advisory Tool
items.client: Training project · WBS module EIOPAN (fictional case company)
items.challenge: Standard product filters do not reliably translate model size, quantisation, context length and use case into a sound hardware recommendation for locally run AI models — risking advice that is either wrong or altogether absent.
items.approach: Hybrid architecture combining a rule-based compatibility engine, versioned fact/benchmark data (RAG) and a language model used strictly for explanation — never for the technical judgement itself. An output validator blocks invented specifications, a reproducible decision record documents every recommendation, backed by four approval gates.
items.result: 100 out of 100 points, rated “absolute professional quality” by the examiner. Hard quality gates fully met: zero invented specifications, 100% source coverage, at least 98% of must-have requirements satisfied. Training project from the WBS AI Consultant program, not a real client engagement.

faq.title: Answered directly
faq.lead: The questions that come up in a first call anyway.

items.q: What role is Marco Strote looking for?
items.a: Both are open: consulting engagements as an independent adviser and a permanent position. Suitable roles include AI consultant, AI governance manager, AI compliance manager, transformation consultant, digitalisation manager, and project or programme lead in a digitalisation context. Interim project leadership mandates are also of interest.
Immediately. As an independent consultant I am not bound by a notice period and can start at short notice, whether on a project or in a permanent role.
All three work. My base is Wentorf bei Hamburg, and I reach the Hamburg metropolitan region daily without difficulty. For projects further afield I am willing to travel and work remotely in between.

items.q: Why the move from sales to consulting?
items.a: It is less a move than a completion. Selling digital and regulatory solutions, I saw over years where implementations actually fail — almost never on technology, almost always on unclear requirements and absent accountability. In 2020 I acquired the methodological side systematically, then immediately led a system introduction as IT project manager. Today I can serve both sides: explain the value and own the delivery.

items.q: What makes the EU AI Act experience distinctive?
items.a: The EU AI Act affects not only organisations that build AI, but everyone deploying third-party AI — they count as deployers and have had obligations since February 2025. Full enforcement begins on 2 August 2026, with fines of up to 35 million euros for high-risk systems. I work at exactly that intersection: AI inventory, risk classification under Annex III, governance structures, and the still unsettled question of how agentic AI can be reconciled with the human oversight required by Article 14.

items.q: Are you an EU AI Act specialist or more broadly positioned?
items.a: More broadly positioned. The EU AI Act is one of several fields — alongside AI strategy, process automation and, since 2026, deepened technical skills in prompt engineering and AI models from an ongoing AI Consultant certification program.

items.q: Don't I also need a data scientist or ML engineer for an AI project?
items.a: Depends on the project. If a custom model needs to be trained or statistically validated, I bring in specialised experts. The role before that — clarifying needs, sharpening goals, translating between leadership, the business and technology — I have covered for 25+ years. I am actively building out the technical integration side: in my AI Consultant certification program I have already delivered several self-built AI applications with top scores. For most organisations, that means an experienced point of contact for strategy and steering, with evidenced technical delivery capability.

items.q: Which industries has Marco Strote worked in?
items.a: Principally chemicals and hazardous materials management (three years in product compliance and product stewardship at 3E, two years at 1WorldSync), laboratory and environmental analysis (LIMS implementation), e-commerce and digital marketing (hmmh AG, For Sale Digital, Akanoo), and across sectors with mid-sized and large organisations in AI and digitalisation advisory. Earlier in his career, also controlling and sales roles in media, travel and building materials (SinnerSchrader, Kabel New Media, Egencia, TBG Nord-Beton).

Fourteen certifications: thirteen from AXELOS and EXIN — ITIL 4 Strategic Leader covering Digital & IT Strategy and Direct, Plan and Improve, plus ITIL 4 Foundation; PRINCE2 Foundation, PRINCE2 Practitioner and PRINCE2 Agile Practitioner; Agile Scrum Foundation, Scrum Master and Scrum Product Owner; EXIN BCS Foundation in Business Analysis together with Practitioner certificates in Business Analysis Practice, Requirements Engineering and Modelling Business Processes — plus the WBS AI Consultant Certificate (expected completion: August 2026).

items.q: What is the fastest way to reach Marco Strote?
items.a: By email at mstrote@yahoo.de or via LinkedIn. I usually reply within 24 hours. A short message with the role or initiative and your intended timeframe is enough for a first conversation.
